_comment: Declarative model routing for Patrick OS. Task classes name work, not vendors.
Credentials are never stored here -- only the NAME of the environment variable
that holds one. Editing this file is how you change which model does what;
no Python change should ever be required to add or retire a provider.

local-qwen._note: Same endpoint Site Factory writes against. The 24k request-body cap is the measured limit of the narrative-sourcing tunnel; it is a routing constraint, not an adapter detail.

hermes-copilot._note: Reuses Hermes' existing credential pool; no API key is copied into Patrick OS. Verified working on this machine 2026-09-03 with gpt-4.1 and gpt-4o. Site Factory's .env points at SITE_FACTORY_JUDGE_PROVIDER=openai-codex, for which `hermes auth` shows NO stored credential here, so that judge path is currently dead. isolate:true adds --ignore-rules --ignore-user-config so a work order does not inherit Hermes' own AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, memory, or preloaded skills.

hermes-copilot-4o._note: A second model on the same Hermes credential, verified working 2026-09-03. Exists so judging is possible at all on a one-provider machine: with only hermes-copilot declared, choose_judge() had nothing independent to fall back to and refused. Same-vendor, same-credential independence is WEAKER than cross-vendor -- it separates the model but not the provider's system prompt or safety stack. It clears the bar Site Factory's own llm_client enforces (judge model must differ from writer model) and no more. Re-authenticating hermes-nous, or setting ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, is the real upgrade.

hermes-nous._note: Present in Hermes' credential pool but its refresh token is rejected as of 2026-09-03: `hermes model` re-auth is an interactive browser login. Left in the table as a declared fallback, deliberately NOT preferred by any route until it is re-authenticated.

openai-api._note: api_key_env is deliberately NOT plain OPENAI_API_KEY: that variable is set to the literal 'local' for the Qwen server in Site Factory's .env, and reusing it would silently send a junk key to api.openai.com.

routes._why: Mining public forums is high-volume and low-stakes. Keep it free.
Anything a human will put their name on gets the strongest writer.
Short public replies: quality matters, volume is low, cost is not the constraint.

Site Factory's hardest-won lesson (SF-07): a judge that shares a model or an answer key with the writer measures nothing. The judge must differ from the writer, by construction. Order is by strength of independence, not convenience: a different vendor (anthropic-opus) separates model, system prompt and safety stack; a second model on the same credential (hermes-copilot-4o) separates only the model, and is the last resort that keeps judging possible at all on a one-provider machine.

Diagnosis is where a seductive but unsupported reading does the most damage, and it is the one stage whose output every later stage inherits. It does not go to the cheap model. This is the same reasoning as the draft route, applied a stage earlier: the difference between a seductive interpretation and a defensible one is the product.
Choosing the intervention is the decision Site Factory was making implicitly by having only one tool. It gets a strong model and, like diagnosis, must be able to conclude that nothing is warranted.
Client material and candidate PII never leave the machine.
